text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected on /v1/chat/generate from 17:03 UTC. Error spikes correlate with increased continuous-batching throughput and KV cache evictions. Paging on-call: @oncall-ryan

oncall-ryan: I'm on it. Seeing 5xx and large latency tail. Reproducing locally against canary shows `InvalidCacheKey` exceptions in prefix_cache. Attaching first logs.

oncall-ryan: Logs:
```
ERROR runtime.prefix_cache: invalid prefix key: hash_mismatch (expected 0x9a3f, got 0x2b7c)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runtime/prefix_cache.py", line 214, in get
    raise InvalidCacheKey(msg)
InvalidCacheKey: tokenizer configuration mismatch
```

sre-anna: Noted. Any recent tokenizer or prompt templating changes? If keys are different that would blow up cache hits and force large KV writes.

ml-ivan: I merged a tokenizer-refactor PR last night (PR #4123). It changed normalization for punctuation -> this will change prompt hashing in a subset of models. I added a migration but maybe it didn't hit all routes.

eng-runtime-sam: If hashing changed, we can either roll back the tokenizer change or add a compatibility layer to accept old key formats. Short term mitigation: disable continuous batching for affected model route and reduce batch size to force direct path and avoid huge prefix materialization.

sre-anna: Agreed. Rolling out quick config change to canary to disable continuous batching and increase cache TTL to avoid evictions while we investigate. Patch snippet I'm applying: 
```
# canary route override
routes:
  - model: text-large-v1
    continuous_batching: false
    batch_config:
      max_batch_tokens: 512
      max_batch_size: 8
cache:
  prefix_kv_ttl_secs: 7200  # bump from 300
```

oncall-ryan: Running rollout now: `redwoodctl deploy --env canary --file canary-override.yaml`

incident-bot: Deploy started by oncall-ryan. Deployment ID dpl-2026-03-15-09:05. Notifying SLO monitor.

support-meera: Observability update: 3 enterprise customers (acct: acme, luminos, finbeta) reported elevated latency and some 500s. Support cases opened. I'm drafting an outbound note for impacted customers.

pm-liz: Please include ETA & mitigation steps. We need a short explanation and that we're prioritizing a rollback if needed.

ml-ivan: I can push a backcompat shim that accepts both tokenization hashes; quick approach: when hash mismatch, try re-hash using legacy tokenizer rules and look up. Risk minimal. I can prepare a patch for runtime today.

eng-runtime-sam: If Ivan can get a small shim build, we can canary it behind a feature flag. But we should be careful with memory — polyfilling will increase KV lookup attempts. Keep TTL high.

sre-anna: Current metrics post-config: 5xx rate dropped from 4.2% to 0.9% in canary; global rollout paused until we confirm. Cache write throughput decreased ~70% on canary nodes. Good sign.

oncall-ryan: Handing off to @sre-anna for next shift. I need to tap out in 20m. Summary posted.

sre-anna: Taking over. Next actions: 1) Get Ivan's shim up on canary behind ff. 2) Run small scale rollback of tokenizer-refactor in non-prod to validate. 3) Prepare rollback plan for prod if shim fails. 4) Customer comms draft.

incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: Mitigation in progress — continuous batching disabled on canary + prefix_kv_ttl increased. Reduction in 5xx observed. Next update in 15m or on major change.

support-meera: Draft to customers (short):
"We're investigating elevated 5xx/errors affecting some chat requests. We've applied a mitigation that reduces user impact while we ship a compatibility fix. We'll follow up within 2 hours with an ETA for a full resolution."

pm-liz: Good. Add a line that enterprise traffic has been routed to resilience tier and that we will offer post-incident credits if SLA breached.

ml-ivan: Pushed shim branch `tokenizer-compat-shim`. Quick test against canary KV: shim returns hits for both old/new hashes. Preparing build.

eng-runtime-sam: Build + canary deploy steps for shim:
```
# build
make -C runtime packages shim-compat
# deploy
redwoodctl deploy --env canary --image runtime:shim-20260315 --ff tokenizer_compat=true
```

sre-anna: Canary with shim deployed. Observing metrics: 5xx down to 0.2% on canary, cache RPS normalized. Memory up ~4% — within tolerance.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated - customer impact reduced. Recommend staged rollout. Please confirm before prod rollout.

oncall-ryan: back from break, ack.

pm-liz: Proceed with staged rollout once QA signs off. Draft to customers updated with ETA TBD -> 1.5 hours.

support-meera: Notifying impacted accounts with current message and ETA.

sre-anna: Rolling shim to 25% traffic now. Monitoring for KV write spikes and new 5xx.

incident-bot: Rolling forward: 25% -> 50% scheduled in 5m.

sre-anna: At 50%: metrics look stable. No regression in memory or latency.

eng-runtime-sam: Kicking off full prod roll in 10m with FF gating. Post-roll we should consider adding a migration job that recomputes prefix keys for warm hot caches to avoid cold thundering later.

ml-ivan: Agreed. I'll open a migration task and a follow-up eval to compare outputs from old/new tokenizers on critical prompt templates.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Full mitigation applied. Monitoring continues. Incident duration ~55 minutes.

pm-liz: Thanks team. Action items:
- ml-ivan: migration job + PR for backcompat permanent solution.
- eng-runtime-sam: add automated test comparing prompt hashing across tokenizer versions.
- sre-anna: post-incident writeup with timeline & customer impact numbers.
- support-meera: customer follow-ups and credits if needed.

sre-anna: I'll own the postmortem and timeline. Draft ETA: first pass in 4 hours.

incident-bot: Incident closed to active responders. Channel will remain for postmortem discussion. :white_check_mark:
